cases.title: image from a url, with a mime type
cases.notes: The baseline. A url is stored as a url and nothing else: no bytes, because none are held and none may be fetched to produce them.

cases.title: image from base64
cases.notes: The one source whose bytes the reference ALWAYS stored, because it is the one that fills the base64 field directly. Before G-53 it agreed on the bytes and disagreed on everything else.

cases.title: image from raw content stores its bytes
cases.notes: G-53, the data-loss row. The reference stored base64 null here unless something had called base64() first, so a message saved before it was sent could not be replayed. Built and serialised with nothing read in between, which is exactly the path that lost the bytes.

cases.title: raw content that is exactly "0"
cases.notes: A payload a truthiness check drops. PHP's falsy "0" has bitten the reference before, and its prompt path still is (trq-0022). A stored base64 of null or "" here means a real one-byte file vanished.

cases.title: audio from base64 is stored as audio
cases.notes: G-53, the discriminator. Without kind, this row and mrt-0002 serialised to arrays that differed only in their bytes, so nothing reading the stored form could tell an image from a recording.

cases.title: video from a url with no mime type
cases.notes: An absent mime type is stored as null, not guessed from the extension and not omitted. Guessing would mean one language sniffing a string another does not.

cases.title: document by provider file id, titled
cases.notes: A reference the provider resolves: an id and a title, no bytes. The title reaches the reference through the factory's argument and the ports through titled(); the row pins that both routes store the same thing.

cases.title: document from text keeps the text
cases.notes: G-53's worst case. The reference stored the title and dropped the document: base64 null, because fromText() holds raw content, and Anthropic's document mapper reads rawContent(), which never cached. The text must survive with nothing read beforehand. Carries a line break and a non-ASCII character so the bytes are UTF-8 rather than ASCII in every language.

subject.title: Notes

cases.title: document from chunks
cases.notes: No bytes and no mime type: the chunks ARE the document, and they are stored in order as a list.

cases.title: a filename survives storage
cases.notes: as() names a payload for providers that want a filename. It is the field a rebuild most easily forgets, because no provider sees it until an upload.

cases.title: a url naming the cloud metadata endpoint is stored, never fetched
cases.notes: G-44's property, carried into storage. The stored form now always carries the bytes a payload holds, and computing them must not become a way to resolve a url: before G-44, reading base64 on this object made the host request 169.254.169.254. base64 null is the evidence. A serialiser that fetched would put the response here, or throw on a runner with no route to that address.

cases.title: a user message carrying an image and a document
cases.notes: Where media is actually persisted. Pins that each part keeps its own kind inside additional_content, in order, and that rebuilding the message rebuilds each part as the type it was rather than as a generic payload.
